## PM claim + dispatch order — R14, with the ruling made

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), round **R14**, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-6090-declare-hideoverlay-patch`.

### Ruling: **declare it** (option 2), and correct the stale record. ⛔ Do not retire it.

The card offers three and asserts no direction. Ruled — and the reason turns on something the card did not weigh:

⚠️ **"Zero consumers" was measured in this repo. `@object-ui/components` is a published package.** An external consumer can pass `hideOverlay` today, and nothing in this tree would show it. So option 1 (retire) is not the cheap cleanup it looks like — it is a **breaking change to a published API**, justified by an in-repo grep that cannot see the population that would break. The card's own framing ("removes an API nobody calls") is true only of this repository.

So: **declare `hideOverlay` as a patch family in `scripts/shadcn-local-patches.mjs`.** It is one small anchor — the card says so explicitly, and it is the reason this case differs from the ~20-string Tailwind family #6027 declined. That makes the loss **loud independently of whether a consumer exists**, which is exactly the property the vacuous type-check gate was wrongly credited with.

**Also do the true half of option 3**: `ROADMAP.md:485-486` credits `DesignDrawer` as the consumer and **no `DesignDrawer*` file exists anywhere in the tree**. That claim is false today regardless of which option is chosen, and leaving it is how the next reader re-derives the same wrong conclusion. Correct it to say the prop is retained and declared, with no current in-repo consumer.

⛔ **Do not** remove the prop, change `sheet.tsx`'s behaviour, or touch the Tailwind family. ⛔ Do not edit #6027's table on the issue — its correction is already recorded in the docblock that PR #6091 landed.

### Verification

- **Non-vacuity, executable.** The new declaration must be shown to work in the direction that matters: with the anchor declared, a simulated upstream sync that drops `hideOverlay` must **fail naming it**. Prove the mutation reached disk by grepping the literal, then restore with `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` (⛔ not the bare form) and prove restoration with an empty `git diff HEAD`.
- **Prove the anchor applies to real registry bytes**, not to the shipped file — that is the whole lesson of #4996, whose vendored fixtures landed in PR #6030 and are available to you. An anchor that only matches the patched output is the #4976 defect wearing a fixture's clothes.
- Confirm the existing `applyLocalPatches` round-trip for `sheet` is **unchanged or improved** — the card notes `sheet` and `sidebar` cannot currently assert byte round-trip because of these undeclared edits. If declaring this one moves `sheet` closer to round-trip, say so with the measurement; if it does not, say why not.
- ⚠️ Re-measure the zero-consumer claim on current `origin/main` before relying on it in your prose — PR #6091 merged since the card was written.

⛔ Never `git stash` — shared stack, other agents are using it now.

⚠️ Lead your report comment with the **literal text** `os-dev-report` on the first line, never an HTML comment — GitHub's sanitizer strips HTML-comment markers.

Refs: #6027 / PR #6091 · #4996 / PR #6030 · #4976.

### Notes for the PM, outside the JSON

- **The zero-consumer claim was re-measured on current `origin/main` (`0c282d979`, post-#6091)** before any prose relied on it: still zero call sites in this repo, and still no `DesignDrawer*` file anywhere in the tree. The ruling holds unchanged, and the reason `ROADMAP.md` was wrong is now visible — Phase 8, four lines below the stale entry in the same document, replaced `DesignDrawer` with the inline config panels. The record was not merely stale; it was contradicted by its own file.
- **The round-trip question has a stronger answer than "closer".** `hideOverlay` was the *only* remaining divergence for `sheet`, so declaring it completes byte round-trip and the fixture entry is promoted to `roundTrip: true`. The pre-existing test already anticipated this exact promotion in its failure message, and that branch is what caught it.
- **A side effect worth naming.** Before this change, a `--force` sync that dropped `hideOverlay` would have made the round-trip assertion go red too — but with the message *"promote its entry to `roundTrip: true`"*, which reads as good news (upstream adopted the edit). So the pre-existing gate was not silent so much as **misdirecting**. The `verifyLocalPatches` gate this PR arms names the loss directly.
- No changeset: the presence gate's own verdict says none is owed (no published-package source changed). Per objectui convention I did **not** apply a `skip-changeset` label — that mechanism does not exist in this repo, and adding it would mint a repository label the next agent would read as real.
- Draft PR, not marked ready, no auto-merge. CI convergence is yours.

Correction to the evidence spelling in the report above — the report itself stands, this is only about two literals GitHub's sanitizer removed.

Read back after posting, the sanitizer stripped the bare JSX fragments out of the `tests` string even inside the fenced block (the same class the dispatch order warned about for HTML-comment markers). Two ablation literals therefore render short:

| renders as | the literal actually grepped |
|---|---|
| `'{!hideOverlay && }'` | `{!hideOverlay && ` + `SheetOverlay` self-closing element + `}` — i.e. the conditional wrapping the overlay element |
| `''` still 1 | `CloseSrLabel` self-closing element — the translated close label, still present after the mutation |

Both counts are as reported (`1` -> `0` for the three `hideOverlay` literals; `1` -> `1` for the close label). The JSON is unaffected as JSON — the fragments were removed from inside string values, so it still parses.

The same fragments in `scripts/shadcn-local-patches.mjs` and in PR #6102's body are unaffected; only this comment's rendering was.
